prose.title: NullKey vs Safe folder in Files by Google | Backup and recovery
prose.description: Compares NullKey and the Safe folder in Files by Google on encryption, backup, recovery, ads, platform and Android versions, using published facts.
prose.thesis: NullKey is an Android app that keeps private notes, documents and photos in an encrypted vault. The Safe folder is a feature inside the Files by Google app that keeps files behind a PIN or Pattern, and the two differ on backup, recovery and supported Android versions.

honest_case.h: The honest case for Safe folder in Files by Google
p: The Safe folder suits readers who already use the Files by Google app and want the lock to sit inside it. Its help page says files can be moved out of the Safe folder after unlocking it, and they go back to their original location. Its Play listing says the Files by Google app has no ads.

It also reaches older devices. The help page says the feature is available for Android 8.0 and up, and the app can be downloaded from the Play Store. NullKey needs Android 12L or later, so it does not run on the earlier versions that the Safe folder supports.

NullKey can create an encrypted whole-vault backup with a read-back check, and it can export single items in a readable form. The Safe folder help page describes moving files out of the folder, back to their original location.

NullKey's recovery key is one you save yourself, and there is no account reset. The Safe folder help page says that if you forget the PIN or Pattern, you cannot access the files. The same help page says Back up to Google Drive is not available inside the Safe folder. NullKey has no cloud sync and declares no internet permission, and you can save its encrypted backup wherever you choose with Android's file picker.

NullKey runs on Android 12L or later and comes from Google Play. The Safe folder is available on Android 8.0 and up, as a feature of the Files by Google app, which can be downloaded from the Play Store.
Both products are described as having no ads. The Safe folder is a feature inside the Files by Google app and not a separate app, so the Play listing statement covers the whole app.

NullKey states its cipher and key handling: AES-256-GCM for stored contents, a random key for each item, and a key derived from your passphrase with Argon2id. The Safe folder help page says the folder keeps files secure using Android storage with encryption.
Neither product was tested for this page; both descriptions come from published sources.

prose.bottom_line: Choose Safe folder in Files by Google if you already use that app, want a lock on specific files, and your phone runs Android 8.0 or later. Choose NullKey if you want a whole-vault encrypted backup with a read-back check and a recovery key you save yourself.

faq.q: Can I get my files back if I forget the lock?
faq.a: The Safe folder help page says that if you forget the PIN or Pattern, you cannot access the files. NullKey uses a recovery key that you save yourself, and there is no account reset.

faq.q: Can the vault be backed up to the cloud?
faq.a: The Safe folder help page says Share and Back up to Google Drive are not available inside the Safe folder. NullKey has no sync, but you can save an encrypted whole-vault backup wherever you choose with Android's file picker.

faq.q: Which Android versions does each one need?
faq.a: The Safe folder is available on Android 8.0 and up, as a feature of the Files by Google app that can be downloaded from the Play Store. NullKey needs Android 12L or later and comes from Google Play.
